facts.text: Erzsébetváros was officially named on 17 January 1882 after Queen Elisabeth, wife of Emperor Franz Joseph I.
The district’s Jewish quarter, once the most densely populated part of Pest, housed the largest synagogue in Europe, the Dohány Street Synagogue.
In 1879 the 7th District Citizens’ Circle proposed naming the area after Queen Elizabeth, a decision that was adopted a few years later.
The New York Coffee House opened in 1894 on Király Street and became a hub for artists, writers, and musicians in early 20th‑century Budapest.
After the 1873 unification of Budapest, Erzsébetváros evolved from a suburb into a vibrant cultural center, hosting cafés, theaters, and nightlife.
During the socialist era, the district underwent significant changes, yet its historic streets and buildings remain a testament to its layered past.
